objectives: Segment taught wh-words into phonemes before spelling.
Use wh at the start of taught words such as when, whip, whiz and wham.
Check the vowel and ending rather than writing only the initial grapheme.
Read each spelling back and recognise who as a separately taught exception.
concepts: Encoding represents spoken sounds with written graphemes.
The wh spelling is used in a set of taught words, even where it sounds like w.
Spelling requires attention to the whole word, not just the first sound.
A word's pronunciation and spelling pattern can vary across English words.

definitions.definition: Represent spoken phonemes with written graphemes.
Separate a spoken word into its ordered phonemes.
A recurring written pattern in words.

workedExamples.solution: Write wh-e-n after hearing and segmenting the word.
Write wh-i-p; check short i and final p.
Write wh-i-z; keep the ending z.

commonMistakes: Writing only w when the taught word uses wh.
Changing the short vowel while spelling.
Assuming who follows the common wh=/w/ pattern.
keyTakeaways: Say and segment the word before writing.
Use wh for the taught initial spelling pattern.
Check the vowel and every ending sound.
Read the spelling back to verify it.
